title: 2004 AMC 12B Problem 5
statement: On a trip from the United States to Canada, Isabella took \(d\) U.S. dollars. At the border she exchanged them all, receiving \(10\) Canadian dollars for every \(7\) U.S. dollars. After spending \(60\) Canadian dollars, she had \(d\) Canadian dollars left. What is the sum of the digits of \(d?\)

solutions.text:
Exchanging gives \(\dfrac{10d}{7}\) Canadian dollars. After spending \(60,\) she has \(\dfrac{10d}{7} - 60 = d.\) Then \(\dfrac{3d}{7} = 60,\) so \(d = 140.\) The sum of its digits is \(1 + 4 + 0 = 5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Exchanging \(d\) U.S. dollars gives \(\dfrac{10d}{7}\) Canadian dollars
